rootDecision.reason: The finite varied-length/optional-branch pattern yields a small, repeatable close-up gain across the reviewed static exterior poses with no strong new defect observed. It is lower complexity than the derivative variant and avoids the clearly rejected engraving, colour, edge and grain experiments. This is not sufficient evidence that the workbench has a unified physical understanding of the lip.

systemAudit.currentCapability: The existing model has native lip rails, material ownership, strain-related detail scaling and separate surface controls.
systemAudit.currentGap: The native geometric grooves, shader micro relief and roughness are still only partially connected; a coherent multi-scale tissue/strain/reflectance model has not been demonstrated.
systemAudit.nextNecessaryQuestion: Can native primary and secondary structure share a single rest-space organization, then produce mutually consistent geometry, normal and roughness responses under stretch and compression?
acceptanceForNextRound: Visible improvement in the inter-groove surface under matched close-up views.
Benefit under more than the neutral frontal pose.

Separate tests for temporal stability if motion stability is claimed.

finalDecision.remainingRisk: Some isolated fine lines in open-mouth and pucker views still risk reading as engraving. Do not further increase their amplitude without new convincing evidence.
